page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.12xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on KVM hypervisors. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz, providing 48 dedicated virtual CPUs. System memory totals 384.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this instance profile.

For network connectivity, the instance provides a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps, facilitating high-throughput inter-node communication and data ingestion. Local block storage is not bundled with the server, necessitating reliance on networked cloud block storage for persistent data requirements. In terms of resource efficiency, the 1:8 compute-to-memory configuration delivers high memory density, minimizing host overhead for workloads constrained primarily by RAM capacity rather than compute cycles or local drive throughput.

Tradeoffs involve the complete absence of local ephemeral storage, which requires all disk operations to transverse the network fabric, as well as the standard 2.7 GHz clock speed, which suits parallelized enterprise throughput rather than maximum single-threaded execution. These specifications make the ecs.r8a.12xlarge suited for in-memory databases, large Redis caches, memory-intensive big data processing, enterprise ERP backends, and memory-bound ETL pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Configured on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, it is paired with 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware profile includes no integrated GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage, depending entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps, supporting stable throughput for data-heavy cluster environments. The instance offers significant memory density per core, delivering operational efficiency for workloads that require large RAM capacities without necessitating proportional scaling in CPU allocation. Given its architectural characteristics, the ecs.r8a.12xlarge is well aligned with memory-intensive applications, including large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise application servers, and complex data analytics pipelines.
